audit_notes: Model: steady 1D conduction through the roof in normalized coordinate x (x=0 interior, x=1 outer surface); since the gradient is taken over the full normalized thickness, roof_u_value*dT_dx is the heat flux in W/m2. Outer boundary is a linearised surface energy balance: absorbed solar (1-SR_aged)*I, convective/linearised radiative exchange h*(T_a-T_s) and net longwave loss eps*R_net. Linear, closed-form solution: dT_dx = [alpha*I + h*(T_a-T_in) - eps*R_net]/(U+h). Parameter checks: solar_reflectance 0.95 clean is consistent with BaSO4/alumina scattering layers (0.95-0.98) at 300 um. aged_reflectance_loss 0.03 as a 20-year average is optimistic for a porous inorganic surface in a dusty hot climate: field data on BaSO4/CaCO3 radiative-cooling paints show 0.02-0.05 loss within the first year and porous surfaces trap fine dust; I raise it to 0.06 (service-life mean aged SR 0.89). thermal_emittance 0.94 is plausible for fine-grained silicate/alumina (hemispherical 0.92-0.95). U=0.5, h=15, I_mean=300, R_net=85, T_a=35 C, T_in=25 C are consistent daily-mean values for a clear hot-dry summer day; note that daily-mean linearisation hides the peak-hour effect (peak q differences are larger) and that R_net of 85 W/m2 applies to dry climates (humid Gulf/tropical: 40-60 W/m2, which shrinks the advantage). Dimensionless: ratio h/U = 30 (outer film much more conductive than the roof, so the roof controls the flux); solar absorption number alpha*I/(h*(T_a-T_in)) = 0.22 design vs 0.66 baseline. Simulation coefficient: effective overall conductance from sol-air temperature to interior U_eff = U*h/(U+h) = 0.484 W/m2K. Hand solution: design dT_dx = (0.11*300 + 150 - 0.94*85)/15.5 = 6.65 K -> q = 3.33 W/m2; baseline (SR 0.85 with aged loss 0.18 -> 0.67, eps 0.90): (99 + 150 - 76.5)/15.5 = 11.13 -> q = 5.56 W/m2; gain ~40 %. Material check: potassium silicate binder is UV-stable and non-combustible; risks are microcracking under thermal cycling (roof surface 10-45 C daily) and on flexible substrates, and water uptake; surface temperatures stay far below material limits. Other benefits (durability) cannot be computed by this steady model. Baseline: the conventional aged white acrylic cool coating as in the map baseline.
